export function build(g) {

}

input.summary:
Pyramid NW parlour (room-14) no longer writes into the stove cells the chimneys part already built: the furnace at x40 y3 z11 and its stone-brick mantle at x40 y4 z11 are dropped from the layout.
The room's remaining furniture is unchanged: barrel cabinet, standing lamp, two chairs, table, and the hanging lantern.
make.sh now reports "room: Pyramid NW parlour: 7 placed" with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE, and it wrote build.nbt.

waste.what: Found which earlier part owned the refused cells by reading the report's coordinates and inferring the chimneys part's hearth_nook; the refused-write line gives no owning part.
waste.cost: one full make.sh run, one grep of the output, and one read of the part file; no blocks placed by hand
waste.tool: Have the runParts refusal line name the part that placed the cell (e.g. 'had: furnace from Chimneys and hearths'). Also, `mcd plan build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "Pyramid NW parlour"` marks already-built cells as 'o', which would have shown the stove before the part was written.

waste.what: Removed three layout characters (furnace, mantle, and the matching blank rows) by hand and re-ran the build to confirm.
waste.cost: three Edit calls plus one rebuild
waste.tool: A layers() dry-run that reports refused cells against the locked grid before writing would have caught this without a full make.sh.
